It was convenient to be so long and Jax, thar when the Fetus in the Womb grows strong, it might not break it by its sprawling and rumbling about; and after ir is born, the Secundine, or Affer - birth, might be drawn out the better by ir. The way that it passes from the Navel ro the Placenta, is very unconstant; for sometimes, it goes upon the Right-hand to the Neck, which having encompafitd, ic descends to the Placenta, and sometimes, it goes on the Left-hand up to the Neck, & c. The foremost and tippermoft is less, and goes into the Cavity of the Shoulder: The backward Process is thicker and larger, ends in an obtuse Angle; acid enters the hinder Cavity of the Shoulder; the Latins call ir Gibber ous: In the middle of thef, there's a great Cavity like a Semicirel.: It has yet another external lateral Cavity for the Head ofthe Radius, or lesser Bone of the Cu bit; it is jointed tthe lower End with the Wrist, both by a Cartilage in the Middle, and by an acute Process, and therefore called Styloides, being like sharp-pointed Pen used in Writing-Tables) whence there arises a Ligament, which fastens the Cubit and the Foynt of the Writ together.

unguisanail.c: UNGUIS, a Nail, isa similar, flexible, whie, and hard Part, which defends the Fingers from external Injuries, and in some measure adornsthem. - The Root of it is joined. to a certain Ligament, and by reason of the neighbouring Tendons it be - Comes sensible: They seem to be made of a Collection of very little Pipes, which adhere extremely thick to one another, and shoot-out into length. Where they begin, there you find certain nervous Fibres like so many small Nipples Jengthen'd, the lengthen'd Parts whereof, are seen as far as the Nail: If they be forcibly torn off, they leave di vers Holes, so that the Horney Substance of th Nails looks like a, Net. Under the Nails there's a pappy sort of Body, which has its Vessels of Excretion.; The Apices, or Tops of the Nails, are they which grow beyond the Flesh; the Parts which are out, are called the Seg mina, the Paring of the Nails; the parts under the Nails, are the xpuale the hidden parts; the white Semi-lunar part next the Roor, is the Rife cf the Nail; the very Beginnings that grow into the Skin, are call'd the Roots of the Nails the Sides, the Clefts; the white Spots, Nubecule, little Clouds, e. Blanchard.
